circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Melbourne's Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling a lake in the city's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support categories and racing series. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, the 4. 326 km Austrian circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and held the country's Grand Prix annually from 1970 to 1987. Following a redesign and shortening of the layout, it reopened as the A1-Ring and returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix between 1997 and 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, measuring 6. 003 kilometers and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar a year later under the Azerbaijan Grand Prix name.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The venue accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2, drag racing, and endurance competitions, while maintaining multiple circuit configurations under its FIA Grade 1 classification.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and hosts the Spanish Grand Prix. This versatile venue features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations, accommodating nearly 141,000 spectators across its facilities while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit, located near the town of Spa in the Wallonia region, stretches 7. 004 kilometers and has been hosting the country's premier racing event since 1950. The venue participated in Formula One's inaugural season and has maintained continuous Grand Prix races from 1985 onward, with only brief interruptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre temporary road course that annually hosts Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various major motorsport series including sportscar championships and open-wheel racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has been the primary venue for China's Formula One Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track also began hosting an electric racing championship event starting in 2024, diversifying its motorsport calendar beyond traditional circuit racing.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit serves as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix, a fixture it has held since 1948. The venue hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950 and, after sharing the British Grand Prix with Aintree and Brands Hatch for several decades, became its exclusive host from 1987 onward.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted Formula One's historic 1986 Hungarian Grand Prix, marking the championship's first appearance in an Eastern Bloc nation. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the Hungarian government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 that ranks among Europe's earliest purpose-built racing venues. The venue has hosted Formula One's Italian Grand Prix nearly every year since 1949, earning its nickname "Temple of Speed" for featuring notably long straights and fast-flowing corners that characterize its high-speed layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, is primarily renowned for hosting Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating major thoroughfares and landmarks of the famous entertainment district. The layout traverses Las Vegas Boulevard and passes iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a track that merges racing with the city's distinctive resort landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two Mexican racing brothers who both died in accidents, Ricardo in 1962 and Pedro in 1971. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards on its current layout, having previously held the race during two earlier periods ending in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track was introduced to the F1 calendar in 2022 for the Miami Grand Prix and serves primarily as an F1 venue, though Formula E adopted a modified configuration beginning in 2025.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street circuit winding through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following routes around the harbour in the principality. The track is officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, though it is frequently called by the name of its primary neighbourhood, Monte Carlo.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track featuring dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners that earned it the nickname "Roller coaster in the Dunes" among fans. The venue hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026, bringing Formula One racing back to the Netherlands after a lengthy absence.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motorsport venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, featuring a 5. 419-kilometer layout with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and an FIA Grade 1 classification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years prior. The counterclockwise circuit features additional facilities including a kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian motorsport legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, situated alongside the Red Sea waterfront. Since 2021, it has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and recently began hosting an electric racing championship in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary racing venue that winds through Singapore's Marina Bay district, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang neighborhoods.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometer circuit near Montmeló features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas near Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 track that annually hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside other major international motorsport events including MotoGP and endurance racing. The facility has established itself as a premier American racing venue, having previously accommodated various series ranging from IndyCar to sports car competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championship titles during his tenure with Renault in 2005 and 2006. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has demonstrated remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and twice triumphing at Le Mans with Toyota, making him the sole driver to achieve both a Formula One championship and a World Endurance title.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver for Mercedes, secured the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship at a record young age. Since making his series debut in 2025, he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. His career has progressed through various racing categories before reaching the sport's pinnacle.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes during 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian motorsport competitor currently racing in the LMP2 category for AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series, while maintaining a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One. The driver has made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025 and previously drove for Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly represents France in Formula One racing and currently drives for Alpine. The French driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory in 2020 at Monza while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple circuit records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One and has demonstrated excellence beyond single-seaters, notably claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has claimed nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport. He achieved his best championship result in 2022 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen has competed across multiple motorsport categories, including a Formula One career spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship, representing BMW as a factory driver for the WRT team.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Throughout his eight-season career in the sport, he has secured 14 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French racing driver who represented Haas in his most recent Formula One campaign. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory with Alpine stands as a significant achievement in his career.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The experienced competitor finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed nine race victories during his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before moving on to other racing ventures. He now races in the FIA World Endurance Championship for Ford, following earlier appearances in the same series with Proton Competition in the LMGT3 category.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing under his commonly used name rather than his full surname Strulovitch.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, held a full-time Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has claimed four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has achieved 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One driver to date, having raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, representing Renault's sports car division while functioning as the manufacturer's official works entry. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025, the team transitioned from its previous identity as Renault F1 Team.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has competed in Formula One across multiple incarnations, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team designation.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing operations of Italian luxury car manufacturer Ferrari and stands as both the longest-running and most accomplished outfit in Formula One history, participating in every world championship since the sport's inaugural season in 1950. The team, famously nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, maintains an unparalleled legacy of continuous competition in the sport.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One outfit in 2014, launching competitive operations in 2016 with a focus on competitive chassis development and driver pairing strategies. The team operates under American registration and has undergone leadership changes, with Ayao Komatsu assuming the principal role in early 2024 following his predecessor's departure.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering outfit achieved considerable success in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. After 32 years competing in the championship, the team departed in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving constructors, having been acquired by Audi AG the previous year to establish the foundation for Audi's factory F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under the ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operating from Brackley under a German licence. The team underwent a significant ownership restructuring in January 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. Mercedes-affiliated racing operations have earned the historic "Silver Arrows" designation throughout their championship history.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team portfolio. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes alongside its sister squad, the team operates as Red Bull's secondary racing outfit within the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as Red Bull Racing's sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's racing portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates under an Austrian licence while based in England, having competed in Formula One since 2005 under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its first two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed the management role in 2025. Red Bull GmbH also owns Racing Bulls, making it a dual-team operation within the sport.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, emerging from the ashes of Williams's prior failed racing venture. Based at a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes under various title sponsorships, including Atlassian Williams for the 2026 season. The outfit remains a significant manufacturer of F1 machinery and constructor of its own competitive vehicles.
